column1: # allocation-proven-extents.tsv - OPUS 2026-09-20. Every call to the four construction/allocation helpers whose
# size argument is an IMMEDIATE, paired with the types that already carry that exact extent.
# 471 sites; 152 of them (69 distinct sizes) have no type of that extent.
# THE FOUR HELPERS, and they are NOT the same kind of thing - do not sum their rows:
#   00244F50  pool-or-heap WIDGET FACTORY, 243 sites. (size ecx, proc rdx, initArgs r8). Size 0 becomes 0xC0; a
#             size above 0x120 skips the pool and takes 002497B0(size); at or below it, it scans the 112-slot
#             fixed pool and constructs in place with pooled=1. All of this is already specified in
#             16-UI/Widget-Object-Model/CONTRACT-widget-object.md sections 2 and 5 - this census does not add it.
#   00245000  PLACEMENT widget constructor, 41 sites. Not an allocator. All 31 bytes are `mov rbx,rcx /
#             mov dword [rsp+0x20],1 / call 002465F0 / mov rax,rbx / ret` - it RETURNS RCX UNCHANGED, so rcx is
#             the OBJECT ADDRESS and the memory is the caller's. 002465F0 is the widget constructor; the
#             hardcoded 1 is the contract's `pooled & 1`, so every 00245000 object has flags bit 14 set.
#             (An earlier header of this file called it an allocator taking a parent. Both were wrong.)
#   002497B0  widget HEAP block, 8 sites - the over-0x120 path out of 00244F50.
#   00210EC0  malloc, 179 sites - via IAT 008C2B40 through 0085E730, established for GameSettingConfig.
# WHAT THIS IS EVIDENCE OF: an extent stated at the construction site, independent of any field census. A field
# census infers an extent from the highest displacement anything touches, which is a floor and can be short; a
# construction states the size outright before a single field is known.
# The instrument validates on cases it was not told about: 0x1110 is exactly ManagerSub0209BE80_8FA0, 0x61F0 is
# exactly ManagerSub0209BE80_AB30, and 003CA860's three placements at rdi+0x2A0 (0x1C0), rdi+0x460 (0x190) and
# rdi+0x5F0 (0x4A0) reproduce WidgetSingleton02B47758_02A0/_0460/_05F0 and their contiguity from the instruction
# stream alone. In each case the store already held the fact; the census agrees with it rather than extending it.
# WHAT IT IS NOT: identification. A size match is a CANDIDATE, never a type - the 0x1 rows match three unrelated
# one-byte types and mean nothing. A row reading NONE says only that no registered type has that extent; it may be
# a buffer rather than an object (0x10000, 0x100000 and 0x17BB000 plainly are), or an object nobody has typed yet.
# HOME_OR_PLACEMENT and PROC COLUMNS (325 and 235 of 471 rows resolved). For 00245000 rows the home is the rcx
# expression at the site - where the pooled widget is BUILT, since that helper constructs in place. For the three
# real allocators it is instead the SINK: the `mov [reg+disp], rax` or `mov [rip+X], rax` within five instructions
# after the call, i.e. where the returned pointer is PARKED, which is the object's home in the owning structure.
# The two are different relations and the column does not distinguish them beyond the helper name - read the
# helper column first. PROC is the rdx argument of 00244F50, the object's procedure.
# Together these make tilings and ownership visible: 003F9F40 builds two 0xD0 widgets at rbx+0xD0 and rbx+0x1A0,
# contiguous; 00293170 parks a 0x102D0 object at rbx+0xC0 behind a null test, with proc 00292390.
# A blank cell means the form was not an immediate-offset expression in the window scanned, not that none exists.
# FOUR EXTENTS ARE CONSTRUCTED, UNREGISTERED, AND MENTIONED NOWHERE IN THE 681-PAGE PROSE CORPUS: 0x17BB000
# (one site, 00186CD0 @001870F3 - 24.8 MB, plainly a buffer), 0x102D0 (00293170 @00293281, home rbx+0xC0, proc
# 0053E380, behind a null test on 02CA8A80). The other 65 unmatched extents each have their size literal appear
# on at least one page - which is a WEAK signal and not evidence that the object is described there, since a hex
# number can appear for unrelated reasons. Only the four above are absent from both the store and the prose.
# BOUNDS: only immediate sizes are seen, so a computed or register-passed size is invisible and this is a FLOOR.
# The size register differs per helper (ecx for three, edx for 00245000) and is read by a backward scan of at most
# fourteen instructions, so a size set further back is missed.
